summary: Every Pattern triggers one extra time on the first spin of each Round.

summary: Pays your current Interest in coins whenever a spin triggers 3+ Patterns.

summary: Whenever a spin triggers 15+ Patterns (retriggers count), you earn 4x your current Interest in coins. Max once per spin.

Counts as a Surgery charm while equipped; discard it to get the three ingredients back.

assumptions: Assumed the modifier is picked evenly among all 10 kinds (Golden, Token, Ticket, Repetition, Battery, Chain, Investor, Rising, Copy, Revenge).

summary: Surgery (Steam + Diesel Locomotive): every Round you finish without earning any coins permanently doubles both the Symbols and Patterns Multipliers.
tip: Fish for empty Rounds: pick 3 spins in a Round you can spare (about 15% end empty, 25% with Depression) and park Luck charms in a drawer. Each success is x4 coins for good.

synergies.why: With no spontaneous Luck, a 3-spin Round ends empty about 25% of the time instead of 15%.
A sacrificed Round ends at once with no coins earned, which should count as an empty Round.
Fishing Rounds are full of empty spins, each a 25% chance to grow all Symbols.
Discard it after the fusion to get both Locomotives back; they grow on the same miss streaks.

Luck +7 on every Round's last spin nearly always scores something.
Two misses in a row trigger Luck +5, which usually breaks the empty Round.

summary: Surgery (Necronomicon + Pentacle): every Symbol has a 10% Rising chance, +1% per spin with 5+ Patterns (up to 50%); a 666 resets the growth.

Retriggers push spins to 5+ Patterns, growing the chance faster.

summary: Surgery (all four Aces): if you score all 7 Symbols at least once in the same Round, every Symbol's value doubles for good.

The engine reads scoredAll over all 7 Symbols as a per-Round rate, so the doubling is valued as permanent growth at that rate.

summary: Surgery (all four battery charms): Red Button charms refill completely before every spin, but every Red Button press doubles your Debt for good.

Every press triggers button charms twice while the debt still doubles only once per press.

Refilled every spin, it invites more presses, and each one adds Limbo's own 100-500% Debt on top of the doubling.

summary: Surgery (Dear Diary + Fidelity Card), triggers randomly (40%): when you buy a Charm, the store slot you bought it from refills with a new one.

A profitable buy (+2 net tickets) that can refill its own slot.

summary: Surgery (Horseshoe + Nuclear Button + Sacred Heart): Red Button charms trigger one extra time per press, with a 30% chance of yet another.

Tickets double every Round, so its multiplier climbs during the Deadline; spend them before it ends.

summary: Start the run with 12 tickets, but Rounds pay 0 tickets for the rest of the run unless an effect changes it.
tip: A fast start: buy 3-4 charms right away. After that, tickets must come from skipped Rounds, selling charms, Florid Traits or Ticket modifiers such as Raging Capitalist.

synergies.why: Ticket modifiers on every Symbol replace the lost Round income.
A 2-ticket source of Ticket modifiers on Clovers.
Turns the 12-ticket start into more tickets at each Deadline's end.
30% of the debt at once helps you end Deadlines early for 4 tickets per skipped Round.
+5 tickets per call.

antiSynergies.why: Its growth needs phone rerolls, which cost tickets you no longer earn each Round.
Holding 15-ticket steps is hard with no tickets from Rounds.

assumptions: Assumed Deadline-end rewards (skipped Rounds, Florid, CloverPot) still pay; only the per-Round payout drops to 0.

summary: Run-long: every Deadline's debt is halved, but you start with only 15 coins, already deposited. Scores can't go to the Leaderboard.
tip: The relaxed-run card: halved debts are worth about double income all run. Expect a slow first Deadline from the tiny start, then it carries you.

effects.text: The run starts with only 15 coins, already deposited at the ATM. Runs with this card can't upload a score to the Leaderboard.

synergies.why: Halved debts are easier to pay early, so you skip more Rounds for its multiplier.
Halved debts make skipped Rounds common, and each one raises its Golden chance.
More skipped Rounds mean bigger Luck triggers next Deadline.

assumptions: '50% easier' read as every debt multiplied by 0.5 (the Hard Mode wiki page calls it a debt modifier).
Assumed the 15 deposited coins replace the usual starting coins.

summary: When a Deadline ends with 6+ charms equipped, one of them is discarded at random, then you get 2 free Restocks.
tip: A drawback card: any Deadline can cost you a key charm. Dung Beetle grows on each forced discard, Vorago can return the lost charm, and drawers let you drop to 5 charms first.

effects.text: When a Deadline ends with 6 or more charms equipped, one equipped charm is discarded at random (before the 2 free Restocks).

synergies.why: Each forced discard raises all Symbols by their base value.
Holds the discarded charm so you can bring it back.
Bank the 2 free Restocks for +4 Symbols Multiplier.
Pays coins whenever an effect discards a charm.

antiSynergies.why: Its slow Deadline-by-Deadline growth is lost if it is the charm picked.
Its stacked Symbols Multiplier can be wiped by a random discard.
Its banked Symbols Multiplier can be wiped by a random discard.

assumptions: Assumed the 2 free Restocks come only when the discard happens (6+ charms equipped).
Assumed only charms on the table count, not those in drawers.

summary: Run-long: every Deadline's debt is doubled. Escaping through the door unlocks a cosmetic Golden Knob for the slot machine.
tip: A pure challenge card: pick it only to chase the Golden Knob with a build you trust. Every target is twice as high, so permanent scaling matters even more.

effects.text: Opening the door (escaping) with this card unlocks the Golden Knob for the slot machine, if you don't have it yet.

assumptions: The Golden Knob is assumed to be cosmetic (it is tied to the 'Omnipotent' achievement).

summary: Run-long: choosing Most Spins doubles the 666 chance for that Round; choosing Fewer Spins halves it.
tip: From Deadline 3, take Fewer Spins on Rounds you can't afford to lose. Devil builds (Baphomet, Gabihbb'h) and Sacred runs, where the odds cover 999s, can welcome Most Spins.

effects.text: The x2 applies to Rounds played with the Most Spins option; picking Fewer Spins halves the 666 chance for that Round instead.

synergies.why: Doubled 666 odds double Above/Below more often.
More 666s mean more Rounds with a doubled Symbols Multiplier.
More 666s mean more Rounds with tripled gem values.
Cancels a 666 while it still counts for 666 charms.
In Sacred Mode, more 999s double your Patterns Multiplier more often.
In Sacred Mode, more 999s mean more forced Jackpots.

assumptions: The engine assumes Most Spins, so the 666 chance is encoded as doubled.
Assumed the same odds change applies to 999s in Sacred Mode.

summary: Run-long: 666s are twice as likely, but hitting a Jackpot refunds all coins lost to 666s earlier in that same Round.
tip: Only for Luck/Jackpot or devil builds: frequent Jackpots refund most losses, and 666 charms like Baphomet trigger twice as often. Holy Bible covers Rounds you can't lose.

effects.text: Whenever you hit a Jackpot, you get back all coins lost to 666s earlier in the same Round.

synergies.why: Twice the 666s means twice the Above/Below doublings.
More 666s mean more Rounds with a doubled Symbols Multiplier.
Luck +10 on the next spin of the same Round; with 5 more Luck it forces the Jackpot that refunds the 666.
Luck +7 on the last spin raises the odds of a late, refunding Jackpot.
Cancels a 666 outright, a safety net against the doubled odds.

assumptions: Assumed the refund only covers 666 losses from before the Jackpot in the same Round.
Assumed 999 odds double in Sacred Mode as well.

summary: When a Deadline ends, a random table charm gets the Devious Trait (+0.6% 666 chance), then a random drawer charm gets a random Trait.
tip: Devious can overwrite a good Trait on the charm it lands on, and the 666 chance creeps up each Deadline. The Collector counts every Trait it adds; Holy Bible guards the extra 666s.

effects.text: Also at every Deadline's end, a random charm inside a drawer gets a random Trait.

synergies.why: Every charm that gains a Trait adds +1 Patterns Multiplier.
Blocks the 666s the Devious Traits add.
The added 666 chance doubles Above/Below more often.

antiSynergies.why: Devious can overwrite the Avid Trait that call gave.
Devious can overwrite the Ambitious Trait that call gave.

assumptions: Assumed a charm holds one Trait, so a new Trait replaces the old one.
Assumed Devious raises 999 odds instead in Sacred Mode.

summary: Run-long: Interest rises +2% at the end of every Deadline (max 16%), but Interest coins are paid only when a Deadline ends.
tip: Plain deposit Interest now pays once per Deadline, so it is weak early. It suits charms that pay your current Interest: Lucky Cat, Chonky Cat and Token modifiers.

effects.text: Interest coins are paid only when a Deadline ends instead of at the end of every Round.

synergies.why: Pays your current Interest on 3+ Pattern spins, and that Interest keeps rising.
Pays double your rising Interest on 7+ Pattern spins.
Token modifiers pay half your current Interest per scored Symbol.

antiSynergies.why: Its +15% fades 3% per Round, mostly gone before the Deadline-end payout.

assumptions: Read 'Max 16%' as a cap on this card's bonus (+2% for 8 Deadlines); it may instead cap total Interest at 16%.
Assumed Cat and Token payouts are not limited to Deadline end.

summary: Run-long: only 6 charm slots instead of 7, but every charm in the store costs 1 ticket less.
tip: Buy often: Fidelity Card stacks for -2 per charm and the first Cigarettes each Deadline is free. Avoid slot-eaters like Nuclear Button or Hourglass; Property Certificate repays the slot.

synergies.why: Stacks: every charm costs 2 tickets less.
Cheaper charms to buy and discard for its growth.
Costs 1, so its first buy each Deadline is free: +base value on every Symbol plus a restock.
+2 slots more than repays the lost one.
Wins back the lost slot, and costs 1 ticket less.
Costs 1 ticket, so each Voucher nets +3.

antiSynergies.why: Its -1 charm space leaves you only 5 slots.
Its -1 charm space leaves you only 5 slots.

summary: When a Deadline ends: 50% chance to discard every charm in your drawers, otherwise each of them gets a random Trait.
tip: Only leave charms you can afford to lose in drawers when a Deadline ends. Skull spawns free drawer charms to bet and Dung Beetle grows on each discard. Don't park Megaphone or Ankh there.

effects.text: At every Deadline's end, 50%: all charms in all drawers are discarded; otherwise every drawer charm gets a random Trait.

synergies.why: Each discarded drawer charm raises all Symbols by their base value.
Traited drawer charms add +1 Patterns Multiplier each once equipped.
Spawns free drawer charms each Deadline (one per Corpse piece) to gamble with.
Pays coins for every charm an effect discards.

antiSynergies.why: Usually parked in a drawer between calls, where it can be wiped.
The drawer trick that saves Ankh for later risks losing it.
A drawer-stored Barathrum and the call it holds can be lost.

assumptions: Assumed a new Trait replaces any Trait the drawer charm already had.

summary: At the start of the run, 2 random Symbols get their chance to appear halved.
tip: Roughly neutral: about -5% to +12% coins depending on the pair (fewer types on the grid form a few more Patterns). Check which two were halved and build around the rest.
assumptions: Assumed the base chance is halved, so later '+1 manifest' boosts still add their full amount.
The -5% to +12% range comes from simulating all 21 possible pairs on a starting board.

summary: From Deadline 3 on, the last Round of every Deadline is guaranteed to show at least one 666.
tip: Pay the debt before the last Round to skip it. Played, its 666 wipes that Round's coins (all held coins from Deadline 7) and turns the next call Red. Baphomet loves a sure 666.

effects.text: From Deadline 3, at least one 666 is guaranteed during the last Round of every Deadline, with the usual 666 coin loss.

synergies.why: A sure 666 every Deadline doubles Above/Below each time.
Doubles the Symbols Multiplier for the rest of that last Round.
Triples gem values for the rest of that last Round.
Cancels the forced 666, which still counts for 666 charms.
+3 spins after the forced 666 to win coins back.
3 free Restocks every Deadline from the forced 666.

assumptions: Assumed the forced 666 counts for 666-triggered charms like a natural one.
A 666 in a Deadline's last Round makes the next call Red (Telephone wiki); in Sacred Mode it may become a 999 instead.

summary: Bans single-Symbol charms for the run: Symbol Pictures and Photo Book, Monopoly Pieces, Catan Tiles and the Golden Symbol charms.
tip: The store then shows more general charms (multipliers, Luck, retriggers). For Golden, Ticket and Token modifiers, turn to Greedy King, Raging Capitalist and Naughty Dealer.

effects.text: Banned for the whole run (listed in the terminal): the 7 Symbol Pictures and Photo Book, the 7 Monopoly Pieces (Ticket modifier charms), the 7 Catan Tiles (Token modifier charms) and the 7 Golden Symbol charms.

synergies.why: With the Golden Symbol charms banned, it is the main Golden modifier source.
Replaces the banned Monopoly Pieces as a Ticket modifier source.
Replaces the banned Catan Tiles as a Token modifier source.

assumptions: Banned list taken from the wiki notes; the in-game terminal is the authority.

summary: Phone abilities trigger twice, but the store starts empty every Deadline.
tip: Phone-centric run: value ticket-free power from calls; restocks become your shop.

effects.text: Store is empty at the start of every Deadline (restock to fill it).

synergies.why: Phone abilities trigger three times.

summary: Run-long: every charm in the store comes with a random Trait (when it can have one). The run starts with 4 tickets.
tip: Traits make most charms pricier (about +1.4 tickets on average), but every buy brings a bonus. The Collector becomes huge: +1 Patterns Multiplier per traited charm.

synergies.why: Nearly every charm you equip has a Trait: +1 Patterns Multiplier each.
Avid and Ambitious Traits turn into x2 multipliers.
Offsets the Trait price increases.
Cancels the 666s that Devious Traits add.

assumptions: Trait odds follow the wiki's forced-Trait table (Florid and Gambler most common, Devious about 14%).

summary: Run-long: Red Button charms trigger one extra time per press, but they no longer regain a charge at the end of each Round.
tip: Build around charge sources: Electricity Meter (each restock), Potato Battery, AA Batteries, Car Battery or Energy Drinks calls. Vorago can return a charm fully charged.

synergies.why: Every restock refills a charge, the main way to keep pressing.
+1 charge to every Red Button charm whenever 2 spins in a row pay nothing.
Battery modifiers refill charges as you score.
A full refill of every Red Button charm.
Restores all charges, worth far more without Round recharges.
A charm it brings back returns fully charged (wiki strategy).

antiSynergies.why: Needs 12 charges and never refills by itself: about one use per run.

summary: Run-long: coins can only be deposited after the last Round of each Deadline, so everything you earn stays in hand until then.
tip: Interest, the Cats and Token modifiers pay nothing with no coins deposited, and you can't skip Rounds. From Deadline 7 a 666 takes your whole stash: guard with Holy Bible or Rosary.

effects.text: Deposits are only allowed after the last Round of a Deadline: Interest (paid on deposited coins) has nothing to work with, the debt can't be paid early to skip Rounds, and held coins stay exposed to 666s.

synergies.why: Doubles your coins every Round, and here all of them are in hand.
Protects the stash you can't deposit from a 666.
35% chance to cancel each 666 that threatens your stash.

antiSynergies.why: Pays your Interest in coins, which is near zero with nothing deposited.
Extra Interest needs deposited coins to pay anything.
You can't pay early, so no skipped Rounds for its multiplier.
You can't pay early, so its Golden chance never grows from skips.
You can't pay early, so there are no skipped Rounds to fuel it.

assumptions: Interest is paid on deposited coins (Interest wiki), so it earns little during the Deadline.
Assumed you can't end a Deadline early, since the debt can only be paid after the last Round.

summary: Start with the Skull and Red Pepper equipped. The store offers at most one box of Sardines, and it always comes with a random Trait.
tip: A free early Luck charm, while the Skull (+5% Debt, can't be removed) opens the corpse-piece path. Traited Sardines are cheap Trait carriers for The Collector and Dark Lotus builds.

effects.text: The run starts with the Skull (can't be discarded, +5% Debt, spawns a free drawer charm per Corpse piece each Deadline) and the Red Pepper already equipped.
The store can offer at most one box of Sardines, and those Sardines always come with a random Trait.

synergies.why: Always shows up in the store with a Trait.
A traited Sardines is a cheap +1 Patterns Multiplier.
Sardines' doubled resell value feeds its Symbols Multiplier.
The Red Pepper breaking counts as a discard.

assumptions: Read 'only 1 box of Sardines' as at most one Sardines offer (wiki Store page).
'Modified' read as having a random Trait.
Skull and Red Pepper are not encoded as effects, so add them to your equipped charms.

summary: Run-long: the coins you pay for a Surgery are refunded right after, so fusing charms is effectively free.
tip: Needs the Surgery Machine (all four drawers unlocked). Fuse spare charms freely: Garbage (any 2), Trash Can (any 3) and Dumpster (any 4) become free permanent boosts.

effects.text: Coins paid for a Surgery are given back right after, so Surgeries cost nothing (you still need the coins on hand to start one).

synergies.why: Any 4 charms into +1 Patterns Multiplier, now for free.
Any 3 charms into +1 Symbols Multiplier, now for free.
Any 2 charms into +base value on every Symbol, now for free.
Spawns free drawer charms every Deadline to feed Surgeries.

assumptions: Surgery requires the Surgery Machine, unlocked after all four drawers (wiki).
Garbage, Trash Can and Dumpster recipes accept any charms (items.json).

summary: Run-long: charms from the store or drawers never have a Trait, while charms spawned any other way always get a random one.
tip: Traits now come from spawns like Help! (Sacred charms), Alexithymia (Evil charms) or Vorago. Store Traits disappear, which hurts The Collector.

effects.text: Charms spawned in the store or in drawers can't have a Trait; charms spawned any other way (phone calls, Vorago, Surgery...) always get a random Trait.

synergies.why: Each Sacred charm it spawns arrives with a random Trait.
Its Evil charm arrives with a random Trait.
The charm it respawns comes back with a random Trait.

antiSynergies.why: Store charms can no longer come with Traits.

assumptions: 'Modified' read as having a Trait.
Which spawns count as 'other' (phone spawns, Vorago, Surgery results) is inferred, not stated.

summary: Run-long: every charm costs one flat price, starting at 1 ticket; each purchase has a 50% chance to raise that price by 1.
tip: Spend the cheap early buys on normally pricey charms (Evil Deal, Megaphone, Barathrum, Cat Food). Every buy can raise all prices, so skip filler and Clover Vouchers.

effects.text: All charms cost the same flat price, starting at 1 ticket; every purchase has a 50% chance to raise it by 1 for the rest of the run (about +1 per 2 purchases).

synergies.why: Normally 50 tickets; here it costs the same flat price as anything.
Normally 7 tickets; cheap while the flat price is low.
Normally 6 tickets; cheap while the flat price is low.
Normally 4 tickets; cheap while the flat price is low.
Normally 5 tickets; cheap while the flat price is low.

antiSynergies.why: Each Voucher you buy can raise every price.
Its repeat purchases keep pushing the flat price up.
Wants many buy-and-discard cycles, which inflate prices.

assumptions: Assumed the price rise is global (all charms), not per charm.

summary: Run-long: every Symbol has a 5% chance to carry the Copy modifier, and store charms never come with a Trait.
tip: Copy turns into the nearest modifier already on the machine, so it pays only with modifier sources: Fortune Teller (Chain), Personal Trainer (Repetition), Greedy King (Golden).

synergies.why: 25% Chain on the grid gives Copy a Chain to become.
25% Repetition on the grid gives Copy a Repetition to become.
Golden modifiers on any Symbol give Copy a Golden to become.
Ticket modifiers on any Symbol give Copy a Ticket to become.
Token, Ticket and Golden modifiers across all Symbols for Copy to mimic.

antiSynergies.why: Store charms no longer come with Traits.

Copy adds nothing when no other modifier is on the machine.

summary: Run-long: phone calls can only be Red or normal (Yellow), never Sacred, so Sacred Mode is closed for the run.
tip: No Sacred calls, Sacred charms, 999s or Good Ending this run. Refusing Red Calls no longer turns the phone Sacred, so Chastity Belt can keep growing past +3.

effects.text: The phone only offers Red or normal (Yellow) calls: it never turns Sacred, so Sacred calls, Sacred charms and 999s are out of reach.

synergies.why: Refused Red Calls never turn the phone Sacred, so its bonus can pass +3.

assumptions: Read 'Red or Yellow' as Red calls or normal calls, i.e. no Sacred calls.
Assumed Red Calls keep coming after 3 refusals.
